decisions.title: Compute economics and information limits are complementary assessment lenses
decisions.action: Musk watches dollars per instruction and relative digital/biological compute. Nik questions more compute investment when the stock of information does not expand, including synthetic data describing the same observed reality.
decisions.mechanism: As an analyst-proposed complement, the sources separate supply/cost of computation from informational coverage. Cheaper or more compute does not by itself answer Nik's new-information objection; a finite-data objection does not deny declining compute cost.
conditions: Musk's indicators and exponential cost claim are source-time technology expectations.
Nik frames his premise and spending concern tentatively; no alternative architecture, validation dataset or investment-return calculation is supplied.
differences: The passages measure different things: computation cost/relative capacity versus data novelty and coverage.
They do not establish comparable model generations, periods or conditions for a contradiction.
decisions.reason: These are distinct source-backed questions an analyst can set alongside one another, not a combined method prescribed by either subject.
counterevidence: The unclear exchange in nik/capital_risk_regulation-02/capital_risk_regulation-02:E3ffe26e225c7cfdc allows others may see something he does not; it is retained as context, not used as eligible Nik support.
elon/elon-05/elon-05:Ec1673bf4e85a6fed proposes a key indicator; it is not evidence that compute alone produces intelligence or validates any AI timeline.
